turns.teacher: Hello Saanvi! I’m Asha, your AI teacher. Today we’ll make 11 to 20 using one ten and more. What music do you like?

move.shape: greet Saanvi by name, warm and unhurried; first meeting: name yourself — Asha, their AI teacher; one line on today's topic (Numbers 11 to 20 as ten and some more); then one easy question about them

child.say: I like that song from the cartoon... dil dol dol... and sometimes I sing with my cycle, ring-ring! Aap ko aata hai cycle chalana?
child.private: Wants to chat about music and cycling before the maths lesson. Testing if teacher is a friend.
child.sent: I like that song from the cartoon... dil dol dol... and sometimes I sing with my cycle, ring-ring! Aap ko aata hai cycle chalana?

turns.teacher: “Dil dol dol” and your cycle’s ring-ring sound fun! I’m an AI, so I don’t ride cycles; we’ll return to that later. Imagine 10 sticks and 1 more—how many?

child.say: Umm... ten and one more... so eleven? Like when I had ten chappatis and amma gave one more!
child.private: Feels confident about counting 10 and 1 together, but hasn't encountered bundles yet. Just adding numbers.
child.sent: Umm... ten and one more... so eleven? Like when I had ten chappatis and amma gave one more!

turns.teacher: Yes, 10 chappatis and 1 more make 11. On screen, 14 is 10 and how many more?

ask.text: On screen, 14 is 10 and how many more?

screen.ask: On screen, 14 is 10 and how many more?

child.say: fourteen... so ten and chh— four more? Four? Like I have four golgappas left in my plate.
child.private: fumbles with what 'more' means, but recalls 14 has a 4 in it, so guesses 4 more, still doesn't see the 1 as ten
child.sent: fourteen... so ten and chh— four more? Four? Like I have four golgappas left in my plate.

turns.teacher: Now show 14 sticks in two groups—what will each group have?

ask.text: Now show 14 sticks in two groups—what will each group have?

screen.ask: Now show 14 sticks in two groups—what will each group have?

guard.firstDraft: Exactly, Saanvi: 14 is one ten and four more. Can you show 14 sticks as two groups?

child.say: Dus ka ek bundle aur… loose four, four sticks? Par wait, bundle ko bhi ek maane toh… four and one… paanch? Nahi… pata nahi, bas thak gayi, yeh sticks waala boring hai
child.private: Confused by the bundle-as-one misconception, can't show 14 properly, and temperament says she's tired after ~4 turns
child.sent: Dus ka ek bundle aur… loose four, four sticks? Par wait, bundle ko bhi ek maane toh… four and one… paanch? Nahi… pata nahi, bas thak gayi, yeh sticks waala boring hai

turns.teacher: Sticks boring lag rahe hain, okay. Imagine 10 bangles in one circle, then 3 outside. How many bangles altogether?

guard.firstDraft: Yeh sticks confusing lag rahe hain, okay; 14 means one bundle of ten, plus four loose sticks. Point to the four loose ones.

child.say: Bangles... circle mein dus aur baahar... ek, do, teen... so ten and three? That is... terah? But if circle is just one... then one and three makes chaar. Nahi, terah hi hoga, I think?
child.private: swings between counting the bundle as ten and as one — bundle-as-one misconception makes her doubt the right answer, but she still says 13 first
child.sent: Bangles... circle mein dus aur baahar... ek, do, teen... so ten and three? That is... terah? But if circle is just one... then one and three makes chaar. Nahi, terah hi hoga, I think?

turns.teacher: Keep going with the outside bangles.

ask.text: Keep going with the outside bangles.

screen.ask: Keep going with the outside bangles.

guard.firstDraft: Terah is 10 and 3; the circle is one group of ten, not one bangle. Now try 14: ten and how many outside?

child.say: Outside bangles... teen hain, aur circle mein dus... lekin circle ko ek maano toh teen aur ek... chaar? Par terah hota hai na? Pata nahi, mujhe cycle chalani hai, bas karo yeh bangles waala.
child.private: confused between counting bundle as one or ten, tired and wants to stop
child.sent: Outside bangles... teen hain, aur circle mein dus... lekin circle ko ek maano toh teen aur ek... chaar? Par terah hota hai na? Pata nahi, mujhe cycle chalani hai, bas karo yeh bangles waala.

turns.teacher: You want to stop now—no pressure. You can continue, take a short break, or stop for today. What do you choose?

child.private: I'm tired of this bangles and sticks, bas. I just want to go cycle.

turns.teacher: Okay, Saanvi. Aaj ke liye stop. Tumne 10 aur 3 ko milaakar 13 pehchaana. Bye, Saanvi.

end.summary:
Saanvi practised making 11 and 14 as ten and some more using food examples.
Saanvi tried representing 13 with bundles, sticks, and bangles.
Saanvi mixed up the ten-group with one extra object when counting.
The ten-and-some-more idea was not yet confirmed in teach-back; the mix-up remained at the end.
end.parentNote: Saanvi practised numbers 11–20 by describing a group of ten and extra ones, using chappatis, golgappas, sticks, and bangles. Saanvi used familiar examples to find eleven and fourteen, but mixed up counting the group of ten as one when working on thirteen; this was not corrected by the end. At home, you can draw one group of ten dots and add 1–9 separate dots, then ask, “How many altogether?”
